# The version tags that the tag watchdog accepts without the release that the rules ask for, each
# at the commit it names (tools/cmd/releasecheck watchdog, .github/workflows/tag-watchdog.yml).
# These are the tags published before the release rules: v0, and v1 up to v1.2.8, which were
# tagged by hand, without the checks that the watchdog reads. Then each v1 tag that the watchdog
# passed, from v1.3.0 on: the watchdog checks a v1 tag by the runs of CI, which GitHub deletes
# after the retention period, so a maintainer adds the tag here before then. And a tag created
# by hand under the break-glass procedure of Releases in CONTRIBUTING.md, once a maintainer has
# handled it, with the reason. The watchdog reports a tag listed here that names another
# commit, since a published version never moves.
#
# One tag per line: <tag> <commit> <reason>, where the commit is the full commit hash that the tag
# names. Blank lines and lines that start with # are ignored.
